items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: I was called by Louis Bellson to make a commercial date with her for an automobile company in Washington

ctx.x: thing that... I've heard Pearl talk a lot about the way she feels about people and certain things, and I often flash back to that, because I never did understand that and she never quite gave me an explanation. And since her climb to fame and everything, words between her and I have been said very sparingly, to like "Hello, how are you?" or something like that.

I was called by Louis Bellson to make a commercial date with her for an automobile company in Washington, and a couple of times when she was on television here I was called on to do some things with her. But the old what was supposed to have been friendship and everything, and closeness, seemed to have disappeared with her career or something like that. I don't know what happened.

But I came back to Washington, and it was another thing of gigging around, a date here with this group or that group, or maybe making up one of my own for a week or a couple of weeks or so. And things got kind of slow from the period of, say, 1950 through about the latter part of 1951. I mean, I wasn't doing anything that pointed in any direction.
